posts.author: ron olson
posts.content_md:
Hi everyone. I just received notice that for the third consecutive year I have won the "People's Choice Award" for best photographer at the San Francisco erotic art show "On the Edge IV" - in spite of ballot-stuffing by my competitors! 

I'm a 3-D photographer to pretty much everyone these days - about the twentieth time Microsoft Word corrected "holographer" I swore off the term at least for the time being.

To any out there who still feel that analog, monochromatic holograms aren't cool, try attending one of my shows and gauging public reaction. I hate to harp but if ever Holotown would wise up to the fact that Q-switched Neodymium based lasers are indeed the way to go - and indeed very expensive - then maybe we could put together a few we'll-equipped communal studios that would offer the viewing public something to get excited about. By the way, my winning image this year was a PG rated glamour/pin-up piece featuring a lovely young woman's face and torso. It is the eye-to-eye engagement absolutely unique to holography that most viewers (to include artists of many different disciplines) point to as most compelling regarding my work. 

Keep your eyes and ears open regarding possible display venues for my erotica - I'm on something of a roll.

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
Great to hear! Please post a picture if possible!

Congratulations!

posts.author: Holomark
posts.content_md:
Congratulations Ron. Good to see you get some accolades for your work.

I must agree that analog, monochromatic holograms are cool - and can be compelling pieces of art.

As to the Q-switched...lasers, I must defer to your judgment and results as I have not had the opportunity to use such equipment. It certainly seems as though it would open the door to more possibilities than when using CW lasers with comparatively low power. Ok you got me, where do I sign up for this "communal studio"?

Not really sure who is disagreeing that faster, stronger lasers such as your Q-switched... can be a good tool for holographers; maybe it is just a touch of jealousy due to the cost of the equipment (not to mention that your models are much more pleasing to the eye than our "porceline cats", "skulls" and the like.)

posts.author: ron olson
posts.content_md:
A few years ago, I offered to make our studio available on a for-hire basis with Bernadette and I to operate the system and holographers and/or would-be holographers to look after the composition and lighting. If memory serves me right, I was offering to charge a fee of around $500 for a two day session with the holographers responsible to supply their own film and chemistry. I did not receive a single response of any kind and I concluded that the issue wasn't really subject matter per se - it was more like a science project that no one wanted to cede control of. 

"I don't care that the images I produce are less than compelling.....as long as I can make them in my basement with my laser-diode."

In a little more than a year our studio lease will expire at which time I will entertain thoughts to relocate the studio to a "neutral site" where I would supply the hardware and other(s) would provide the requisite studio space. It would by necessity be a commercial setting (nobody's home) with access to a large population base. I would rate the San Francisco/Bay Area as most desirable and Southern California as my second choice. Just something for people to be thinking about.

Ed, can I post a topless image on this site?

Oddly, even this web site raises a flag over the use of "holographer".

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
It's fine with me, but I don't own the site. Why not see what happens? The worst that can happen is it will be taken down.

But I should hope not. It is a figure study, after all. There's plenty on another site that I haunt, [http://www.collodion.com](http://www.collodion.com), which may be of interest to others on this site, as it seems to be populated by maniacs as obsessed like us on finicky image-making processes, only addicted to the intoxicating aromas of ether and alcohol and big brass lenses as opposed to lasers and PBQ!

There is of course a difference between erotic and porn!

posts.author: hologram4d
posts.content_md:
Hi Gang, I certainly don’t think this post got the attention it deserved. 

Hey Ron, great to see you are still getting the recognition, keep the (green) flame burning! So hey, yeah, I’m all for your idea of “a few well-equipped communal studios”, and since I just happen to have access to what I believe are (someone correct me if I’m wrong?) the only other two pulsed-green studios in North America (1. Nashville Indiana- has presently been in storage for the last five years, 2. St. Charles Missouri- Allen Fox Studio) I think that makes up the commune for now. 

For God’s sake let’s get some use out of these wonderful lasers! Ron, Allen, and I aren’t exactly spring chickens anymore and we are definitely due for some new blood in the field! For serious, artistic, pictorial holography, Ron is indeed correct, these things can’t be beat! No, they are not the be-all, end- all out there for holography artists, but essential for specific content generation. It amazes me to this day that display holography in general, and specifically “pulsed green” cannot garner the sustained acclaim for a few small “well-equipped communal studios” to collectively operate out there!!?? We now have a whole new generation of folks that have never even seen these things, they’re going to go ape!!! It was never supposed to be some “secret exclusive club”. I think Ron is being pretty stand-up (and cheap) with his generous offer. HOLO Artist’s out there should take him up on this... hell, you can’t even rent a *photography studio* on the west coast for that price! Let’s start seeing some arising, inspiring, creative new work! I’m in till the end, so however we want to work this thing is fine with me. I just want to see people working together, making holograms that are getting shown (and sold), and perpetuating the craft in a much larger arena than it is presently. Kumbaya, anyone?

 With all that said, I have been still kicking some stuff out lately, getting to work with some cool people on some cool projects but there could be so much more! 

My two cents worth (and a couple of big-a** lasers),

Rob Taylor

Forth Dimension

PS- Danny, I think you are missing the point my man... while I cannot deny the appeal of youthful mammary glands as content in holograms... it is indeed the ability *to image living organic form of all kinds* in larger hologram sizes that makes this a no-brainer.

PSS- And in case anyone wants to sell their house and start their own commune, one of the above mentioned pulsed studios can be yours... at around 125K.
